text:
sara: FYI during magnet-64k-int4 onboarding I found a reproducible token drop when streaming after huge prefill. Repro on two machines (gpu-pool-c, gpu-pool-d).
liam: quick tl;dr  are tokens missing, or garbled output?
anika: missing contiguous tokens near the tail of the prefill window; generation resumes after a gap. Not just misranked logits. :confused:
sara: here's the minimal loop I used locally: 
```bash
# short repro loop
for L in 62000 63000 64000 64768; do
  python reproduce_prefill.py --model magnet-64k-int4 --prefill $L --quant int4 --streaming true 
done
```
liam: do you see any shard-boundary correlation?
sara: yes  failures align to when (prefill_length % 2048) in the ~60k range and when rotary_scale != 1.0. Also more likely on shard 2/5.
matt: tried other quant modes?
sara: float32: no failures. int8: flaky (~5%). int4: ~100% on those lengths in our env.
liam: likely a timing/order issue in the quant path (memcpy / compact / stream ordering). Any logged handshake state?
sara: captured state dumps right before stream_start. Example filtered log: 
```
[2026-02-03T14:12:44Z] prefill complete: len=64000, shard=2
[2026-02-03T14:12:44Z] kv: epoch=85 fp=0x9ef1
[2026-02-03T14:12:44Z] transitioning -> stream_start
[2026-02-03T14:12:44Z] stream recv tokens 63990..63998
[2026-02-03T14:12:44Z] ERROR dropped tokens 63998..64005
[2026-02-03T14:12:44Z] stream resumed at 64005
```
anika: dropped range looks like a small rotation/trim during the host-side transition window. Could be async memcpy not finished while we started the stream consumer.
liam: any diffs in epoch/fingerprint between prefill and stream?
sara: I recorded this small diff when failing: 
```json
{"prefill_epoch": 85, "stream_epoch": 86, "prefill_fp": "0x9ef1", "stream_fp": "0x9ef1"}
```
liam: epoch bumped but fingerprint same  suggests buffer swap but identical contents; index mapping may have moved.
matt: try forcing a barrier before stream_start as a canary (env KV_PREFILL_BARRIER=1) and rerun. Also try ROPE_SCALE=1.0 vs 0.998 to confirm scale sensitivity.
sara: did that: ROPE_SCALE=1.0 reduces frequency but doesn't remove it at 64k. Setting KV_PREFILL_BARRIER=1 eliminates the dropped tokens.
anika: that strongly implies race between device-side copy/compaction and host transition. The int4 codepath uses fused kernels on secondary streams which may not be synchronized.
liam: good narrow. For immediate mitigation let's gate the int4 prefill path to use an explicit cudaEvent signal or the KV_PREFILL_BARRIER flag while we fix ordering. Also add a runtime assert that logs when prefill_epoch != stream_epoch.
sara: opened a tiny canary PR to enable KV_PREFILL_BARRIER behind runtime flag and added the epoch assert + extra telemetry fields (rotary_scale, quant_mode, shard_id). Rolling to canary cluster.
matt: I'll profile with nsight timeline on gpu-pool-d tomorrow to confirm missing cudaEvent record or premature host-side callback.
liam: longer term we should audit all async memcpy/compact calls in quant pipeline and prefer event-based sync vs host-blocking.
anika: also add a short onboarding test that runs a 5-10 loop over those lengths for quantized models to catch regressions.
sara: created INF-2987 with repro scripts, logs, and PR link. Canary deploy scheduled.
devbot: Deploy bot: canary rollout queued 2026-02-03T18:00Z by sara.
liam: thanks. Matt, can you drop the nsight capture into the ticket when done?
matt: will do. If the barrier costs too much we'll iterate on event-only sync.
sara: monitoring canary now; will post observations.
anika: great triage. Please update model-onboard checklist to include "long-prefill async racecheck (quant)".
sara: added. Will follow up with perf numbers post-canary.
matt: :+1:
